notes.example:
Synonimy: I am writing to request a referral for / I would like to refer

I am writing to refer Mr Kowalski, a 54-year-old man with a two-week history of exertional dyspnoea.
I am writing to refer this patient for further specialist assessment of her chronic abdominal pain.
I am writing to refer Mrs Smith to your outpatient clinic for urgent review.

Synonimy: I would be grateful if you could arrange / I am writing to ask for

I am writing to request an urgent outpatient appointment for this patient.
I am writing to request further investigation of his persistent haematuria.
I am writing to request your assessment regarding suitability for surgery.

Synonimy: given / considering / in view of

In light of these findings, I would recommend urgent referral to gastroenterology.
In light of her deteriorating renal function, the medication dose was reduced.
In light of the imaging results, surgery was deemed necessary.

Synonimy: as a result / therefore / accordingly

Consequently, his medication was changed to a lower-dose alternative.
The patient missed several follow-up appointments; consequently, her condition worsened.
Consequently, we would appreciate your prompt assessment.

notes.front: should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me
notes.back: w razie pytań proszę o kontakt
notes.example:
Synonimy: please feel free to contact me / do get in touch if you require further information

Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me on the number above.
Should you have any questions regarding this referral, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Should you have any questions about her medication history, please do not hesitate to contact me.

notes.front: I would be grateful if you could...
notes.example:
Synonimy: I would appreciate it if you could / I kindly request that you

I would be grateful if you could see this patient at your earliest convenience.
I would be grateful if you could review his medication regime.
I would be grateful if you could arrange further imaging.

Synonimy: attached is / I have enclosed

Please find enclosed a copy of her recent blood results.
Please find enclosed the discharge summary from her recent admission.
Please find enclosed his most recent imaging report.

Synonimy: with this in mind / for this purpose

To that end, I have arranged for a follow-up ultrasound in four weeks.
To that end, we would ask that his blood pressure be monitored weekly.
To that end, physiotherapy input has already been arranged.

Synonimy: regarding / concerning / in relation to

With regard to her ongoing pain management, please continue the current regime.
With regard to his surgical history, he underwent an appendicectomy in 2019.
With regard to the imaging findings, further correlation with symptoms is advised.

Synonimy: it should be noted that / notably

It is worth noting that she has a family history of colorectal cancer.
It is worth noting that his symptoms improved significantly with the new medication.
It is worth noting that no previous imaging is available for comparison.

Synonimy: at the time of discharge / on discharge

Upon discharge, she was prescribed a five-day course of antibiotics.
Upon discharge, the patient was advised to avoid heavy lifting for six weeks.
Upon discharge, follow-up was arranged with his GP in two weeks.

Synonimy: for reference / to keep you informed

For your information, a copy of this letter has been sent to the patient.
For your information, his previous scan was performed in March 2025.
For your information, the patient's next of kin has been informed.

Synonimy: please advise / please let me know

Kindly advise if any further tests are required prior to his appointment.
Kindly advise on the most appropriate management plan going forward.
Kindly advise if you require any additional clinical information.

Synonimy: as noted above / as stated earlier

As previously mentioned, she has a documented allergy to penicillin.
As previously mentioned, his symptoms began approximately three weeks ago.
As previously mentioned, conservative management was trialled without success.

Synonimy: given the above / taking the above into account

In view of the above, I would recommend an urgent surgical opinion.
In view of the above, her medication has been adjusted accordingly.
In view of the above, further outpatient follow-up is advised.

notes.front: I am pleased to report that
notes.example:
Synonimy: I am glad to inform you that / it is encouraging to note that

I am pleased to report that his symptoms have resolved completely.
I am pleased to report that she responded well to the treatment.
I am pleased to report that his recovery has been uneventful.

Synonimy: on the basis of these findings / in light of these results

Given the above findings, I would suggest a change in her antihypertensive regime.
Given the above findings, further investigation is warranted.
Given the above findings, I recommend a multidisciplinary team discussion.

Synonimy: as soon as possible / promptly

I would be grateful if you could see this patient at your earliest convenience.
Please could you arrange the appointment at your earliest convenience.
We would appreciate a review at your earliest convenience given the urgency.

notes.front: thank you for taking the time to review this referral
notes.back: dziękuję za poświęcenie czasu na rozpatrzenie skierowania
notes.example:
Synonimy: thank you for your attention to this matter / I appreciate your consideration

Thank you for taking the time to review this referral.
Thank you for taking the time to review this referral; I look forward to your response.
Thank you for taking the time to review this referral and for your continued care of this patient.

Synonimy: feeling generally unwell / lack of wellbeing

He presented with a two-day history of malaise and low-grade fever.
She reported general malaise alongside joint pain.
The malaise gradually resolved following a course of antibiotics.

Synonimy: fatigue / tiredness / low energy

The mother reported increasing lethargy in her child over the past 24 hours.
He described several weeks of lethargy and reduced appetite.
Lethargy is a common but non-specific presenting symptom.

Synonimy: shortness of breath / breathlessness

He reports worsening dyspnoea on exertion over the past month.
She was admitted with acute dyspnoea and chest tightness.
His dyspnoea limits him to walking short distances on the flat.

Synonimy: irregular heartbeat / racing heart

She describes intermittent palpitations lasting several minutes at a time.
The palpitations are associated with light-headedness.
He denies any chest pain but reports occasional palpitations.

Synonimy: pain on palpation / sensitivity to touch

There was marked tenderness in the right upper quadrant.
Mild tenderness was noted over the lumbar spine.
No tenderness was elicited on abdominal palpation.

Synonimy: swelling / bloating / enlargement

The abdomen was noted to be distended, with generalised tenderness.
Abdominal distension had progressively worsened over three days.
There was no evidence of bowel distension on the scan.

Synonimy: redness / skin reddening

There was erythema surrounding the surgical wound.
The affected area showed erythema and mild swelling.
No erythema or discharge was noted at the injection site.

Synonimy: paleness / pale complexion

The patient appeared pale, with noticeable pallor of the conjunctivae.
Pallor and tachycardia raised concern for significant blood loss.
There was no pallor or cyanosis on general inspection.

Synonimy: fainting / loss of consciousness (transient)

He experienced a syncopal episode while standing at the bus stop.
She was referred following a single episode of syncope.
The syncope was preceded by light-headedness and blurred vision.

Synonimy: gradual onset / slow-developing

The pain had an insidious onset over several weeks.
Symptoms of insidious onset are typical of this condition.
Unlike acute presentations, this was of insidious onset.

Synonimy: episodic / on-and-off / recurrent

He describes intermittent abdominal pain over the past month.
The symptoms are intermittent rather than constant.
Intermittent claudication was reported on walking uphill.

Synonimy: referred pain / pain spreading to

The chest pain was radiating to his left arm and jaw.
She reported lower back pain radiating down her right leg.
The pain radiates from the epigastrium through to the back.

Synonimy: fever / elevated temperature

The patient was pyrexial on admission, with a temperature of 38.6°C.
Pyrexia resolved following the administration of antipyretics.
He remained pyrexial despite broad-spectrum antibiotics.

Synonimy: feeling sick and being sick / N&V

She presented with a two-day history of nausea and vomiting.
The nausea and vomiting settled with antiemetic treatment.
He reports nausea but denies any episodes of vomiting.

Synonimy: foul-smelling / offensive-smelling

The wound discharge was noted to be malodorous.
She reported malodorous vaginal discharge for one week.
There was malodorous drainage from the surgical site.

Synonimy: swelling / fluid retention

There was bilateral pitting oedema of the lower limbs.
Periorbital oedema was noted on examination.
The oedema improved following diuretic treatment.

Synonimy: poor appetite / reduced oral intake

He describes a three-week history of anorexia and weight loss.
Anorexia was accompanied by early satiety.
Her appetite has improved, with resolution of the earlier anorexia.

Synonimy: itching / itchiness

She complains of generalised pruritus, worse at night.
The pruritus was associated with a widespread rash.
Pruritus can be a symptom of underlying liver disease.

Synonimy: shivering episodes / shaking chills

He experienced rigors associated with a spiking temperature.
The patient reported rigors the night prior to admission.
Rigors and pyrexia raised suspicion of sepsis.

Synonimy: excessive sweating / profuse sweating

The patient was noted to be cool and clammy, with marked diaphoresis.
Diaphoresis accompanied the episode of chest pain.
She reported night-time diaphoresis over the past month.

Synonimy: light sensitivity

He reports headache associated with photophobia and neck stiffness.
Photophobia was a prominent feature of her migraine.
There was no photophobia or neck stiffness on examination.

Synonimy: rapid heart rate / elevated pulse

He was tachycardic on arrival, with a heart rate of 128 beats per minute.
The tachycardia settled following adequate fluid resuscitation.
Sinus tachycardia was noted on the ECG.

Synonimy: slow heart rate / low pulse

The patient developed bradycardia following the procedure.
Bradycardia was attributed to beta-blocker therapy.
He remained asymptomatic despite mild bradycardia.

Synonimy: low blood pressure

He became hypotensive shortly after induction of anaesthesia.
The hypotension responded well to intravenous fluids.
Postural hypotension was confirmed on lying and standing measurements.

Synonimy: fever of unknown origin (FUO)

She was referred for further investigation of pyrexia of unknown origin.
Extensive work-up failed to identify a cause for his PUO.
PUO was eventually attributed to an occult abscess.

Synonimy: muscle guarding / involuntary abdominal rigidity

There was marked abdominal guarding in the right iliac fossa.
Guarding and rebound tenderness raised concern for peritonitis.
No guarding was elicited on gentle palpation.

Synonimy: Blumberg's sign / peritonism

Rebound tenderness was positive over McBurney's point.
The presence of rebound tenderness prompted an urgent surgical review.
There was no rebound tenderness on examination.

Synonimy: icterus / yellowing of the skin and eyes

He presented with painless jaundice and dark urine.
Jaundice was noted on examination of the sclerae.
The jaundice gradually improved following biliary drainage.

Synonimy: bluish discolouration / hypoxic discolouration

Central cyanosis was noted around the lips.
Peripheral cyanosis of the fingertips was observed in the cold.
There was no cyanosis, and oxygen saturations were normal.

Synonimy: digital clubbing

Mild finger clubbing was noted, raising suspicion of chronic lung disease.
There was no evidence of clubbing on examination of the hands.
Clubbing can be associated with a variety of cardiopulmonary conditions.

Synonimy: coughing up blood

He was referred urgently following an episode of haemoptysis.
She reported small volumes of haemoptysis over several days.
Massive haemoptysis required urgent bronchoscopy.

Synonimy: vomiting blood

He was admitted following an episode of haematemesis.
The haematemesis prompted urgent endoscopic assessment.
She denied haematemesis but reported dark stools.

Synonimy: black, tarry stools

He described a two-day history of melaena.
Melaena is suggestive of an upper gastrointestinal bleed.
There was no melaena or fresh rectal bleeding reported.

Synonimy: painful urination

She reported dysuria and increased urinary frequency.
Dysuria and fever raised suspicion of a urinary tract infection.
There was no dysuria or haematuria reported.

Synonimy: excessive urination

He presented with polyuria and polydipsia over several weeks.
Polyuria was one of the initial presenting features of his diabetes.
The polyuria resolved with improved glycaemic control.

Synonimy: increased frequency of micturition

She complains of urinary frequency, particularly at night.
Urinary frequency was associated with mild suprapubic discomfort.
There was no urinary frequency or urgency reported.

Synonimy: infrequent bowel movements

He reports a two-week history of constipation.
The constipation improved following dietary modification.
She denies any recent constipation or change in bowel habit.

Synonimy: loose stools / frequent bowel movements

She presented with a five-day history of diarrhoea.
The diarrhoea was associated with abdominal cramping.
His diarrhoea settled following cessation of the antibiotic.

Synonimy: unexplained weight loss

He reports unintentional weight loss of approximately 6kg over three months.
Unintentional weight loss is a recognised red-flag symptom.
She denies any deliberate dieting to account for the weight loss.

Synonimy: generalised tiredness and unwellness

She presented with several weeks of malaise and fatigue.
Malaise and fatigue were the predominant presenting symptoms.
His malaise and fatigue improved following correction of his anaemia.

Synonimy: vertigo (if rotational) / feeling faint

He describes episodes of light-headedness on standing.
The dizziness was associated with mild nausea.
She denies true vertigo but reports intermittent light-headedness.

Synonimy: disorientation / altered mental state

The family reported acute confusion over the preceding 24 hours.
His confusion resolved following treatment of the underlying infection.
She was noted to be intermittently confused, particularly at night.

Synonimy: decreased consciousness / drowsiness

He was brought in with a reduced level of consciousness following a fall.
A reduced level of consciousness prompted urgent airway assessment.
Her level of consciousness improved following correction of hypoglycaemia.

Synonimy: focal / diffuse (pain)

The pain was localised to the right upper quadrant.
He described generalised abdominal pain rather than a specific focus.
The tenderness was localised, without generalised peritonism.

Synonimy: stabbing (sharp) / aching (dull)

She described the pain as sharp and stabbing in nature.
He reported a dull, constant ache in the lower back.
The pain changed from a dull ache to a sharp, severe pain.

Synonimy: cramping pain / spasmodic pain

He described colicky abdominal pain occurring in waves.
The colicky pain was associated with vomiting.
Colicky pain radiating to the groin is typical of renal colic.

Synonimy: on palpating the area / to palpation

On palpation, a firm mass was noted in the left flank.
The abdomen was soft on palpation, with no organomegaly.
Tenderness was elicited on palpation of the epigastrium.

Synonimy: to be started on / to be initiated on

He was commenced on a five-day course of amoxicillin.
She was commenced on low-dose aspirin for secondary prevention.
The patient was commenced on insulin during the admission.

Synonimy: to be gradually discontinued / to be tapered off

He was gradually weaned off the oxygen supplementation.
Steroids were weaned off over a period of six weeks.
She was successfully weaned off ventilatory support.

Synonimy: non-surgical management / watchful waiting

A trial of conservative management was opted for in the first instance.
Given the mild symptoms, conservative management was appropriate.
Conservative management failed, and surgical intervention was required.

Synonimy: to be assessed / to be seen (by a specialist)

The patient will need to be reviewed in the outpatient clinic in six weeks.
He should be reviewed by cardiology prior to discharge.
She was reviewed by the on-call registrar overnight.

Synonimy: to worsen / to decline

His condition began to deteriorate rapidly overnight.
Despite treatment, her renal function continued to deteriorate.
The wound showed no signs of deterioration on review.

Synonimy: to settle / to become stable

His observations stabilised following fluid resuscitation.
Her condition has now stabilised and she is fit for discharge.
Blood pressure stabilised within normal range after treatment.

Synonimy: preventive treatment / prevention

He was commenced on prophylaxis against deep vein thrombosis.
Antibiotic prophylaxis was given prior to the procedure.
Prophylaxis is recommended in patients with recurrent infections.

Synonimy: not recommended / unsuitable (for a treatment)

This medication is contraindicated in patients with renal impairment.
Given her allergy, penicillin-based antibiotics are contraindicated.
The procedure was contraindicated due to his bleeding disorder.

Synonimy: concordance with treatment

Poor adherence to treatment may explain the recurrence of symptoms.
He reports good compliance with his current medication regime.
We discussed the importance of adherence to reduce future complications.

Synonimy: to gradually adjust the dose

The insulin dose was titrated according to daily blood glucose readings.
Analgesia was titrated to achieve adequate pain control.
The medication was titrated up slowly to minimise side effects.

Synonimy: review appointment / follow-up visit

Follow-up has been arranged in the outpatient clinic in four weeks.
She will require regular follow-up to monitor disease progression.
No further follow-up is required at this stage.

Synonimy: referral letter / request for specialist opinion

I am making this referral for further specialist assessment.
A referral to the pain clinic has been arranged.
The referral was accepted, and an appointment has been scheduled.

Synonimy: coexisting conditions / associated medical conditions

His significant co-morbidities include type 2 diabetes and hypertension.
Given her multiple co-morbidities, a cautious approach is advised.
There were no significant co-morbidities of note.

Synonimy: starting point / pre-existing level

Renal function has returned to baseline following treatment.
His baseline mobility is with the aid of a walking stick.
Repeat imaging showed no change compared with the baseline scan.

Synonimy: to be sent home with

He was discharged with a course of oral antibiotics.
She was discharged with outpatient follow-up arranged.
The patient was discharged with clear safety-netting advice.

Synonimy: to be admitted to the care of

He was admitted under the general surgical team for observation.
She was admitted under cardiology for further investigation.
The patient was admitted under the medical team overnight.

Synonimy: to improve / to fine-tune management

His diabetic control was optimised prior to surgery.
We aim to optimise her pain management before discharge.
Medication was adjusted to optimise blood pressure control.

Synonimy: to settle / to clear up

His symptoms fully resolved within 48 hours of treatment.
The swelling had largely resolved by the follow-up appointment.
Her fever resolved following the course of antibiotics.

Synonimy: to start treatment based on clinical judgement (pending results)

Antibiotics were commenced empirically pending culture results.
Treatment was commenced empirically given the clinical suspicion of infection.
He was started empirically on broad-spectrum cover.

Synonimy: without complications / straightforward

His postoperative recovery was uneventful.
The remainder of her hospital stay was uneventful.
She had an uneventful recovery and was discharged on day three.

Synonimy: family doctor / primary care physician

Please could you arrange follow-up with his GP in two weeks.
The patient was referred by her GP for further assessment.
A copy of this letter will be sent to the patient's GP.

Synonimy: senior specialist / attending physician

The consultant reviewed the patient on the ward round.
This decision was made in discussion with the consultant in charge.
She will be seen by the consultant at her next outpatient appointment.

Synonimy: senior trainee doctor

The on-call registrar was asked to review the patient overnight.
He was initially assessed by the surgical registrar in A&E.
The registrar discussed the case with the consultant before proceeding.

Synonimy: emergency department / ED

He presented to A&E with acute chest pain.
She was brought to A&E by ambulance following a fall.
The patient was discharged from A&E with safety-netting advice.

Synonimy: multidisciplinary meeting

This case was discussed at the weekly MDT meeting.
The MDT recommended proceeding with surgical resection.
Her case will be presented at the next oncology MDT.

Synonimy: discharge letter

Please find enclosed a copy of his discharge summary.
The discharge summary outlines his medications and follow-up plan.
A discharge summary was sent to the GP on the day of discharge.

Synonimy: protection of vulnerable individuals

A safeguarding referral was made in light of the concerns raised.
The safeguarding team was informed of the family circumstances.
Safeguarding concerns should always be documented clearly.

Synonimy: daily patient review by the team

The patient was reviewed on the morning ward round.
His plan was updated following discussion on the ward round.
She was noted to be clinically improving on the ward round.

Synonimy: closest relative / primary contact

The next of kin was informed of the change in his condition.
Contact details for her next of kin are recorded in the notes.
We discussed the treatment plan with the patient's next of kin.

Synonimy: management plan

A comprehensive care plan was agreed with the patient and family.
The care plan includes regular community nurse visits.
His care plan was reviewed and updated following the recent admission.

Synonimy: temporary/covering doctor

The locum consultant reviewed the case overnight.
A locum GP was covering the practice that week.
He worked as a locum registrar during his first year in the UK.

Synonimy: outpatient appointment / OPD

She was seen in the out-patient clinic six weeks after surgery.
An appointment has been arranged in the respiratory out-patient clinic.
He was discharged from the out-patient clinic following full recovery.

Synonimy: hospitalised patient

He remained an in-patient for a total of five days.
As an in-patient, she received daily physiotherapy input.
In-patient management was preferred given the severity of symptoms.

Synonimy: initial assessment and prioritisation

He was triaged as a priority case on arrival.
The triage nurse assessed his observations on arrival.
Triage helps prioritise patients according to clinical urgency.

Synonimy: district nurse

The community nurse will visit twice weekly to change the dressing.
A referral was made to the community nursing team for wound care.
Community nurse input has been arranged to support her at home.

Synonimy: to put someone's mind at rest / to comfort

I reassured her that the findings were benign.
He was reassured that this is a common and treatable condition.
We aimed to reassure the family throughout the procedure.

Synonimy: to explain in simple/plain language

I explained the diagnosis in layman's terms to ensure understanding.
It is important to explain procedures in layman's terms before consent.
He appreciated having the results explained in layman's terms.

Synonimy: consent following full explanation

Informed consent was obtained prior to the procedure.
We discussed the risks and benefits to ensure informed consent.
The patient gave informed consent after all questions were answered.

Synonimy: to deliver difficult news

Breaking bad news requires sensitivity and clear communication.
I broke the news to the family in a private, quiet room.
He was supported by a nurse while receiving the bad news.

Synonimy: pros and cons / advantages and disadvantages

We discussed the risks and benefits of the proposed treatment.
The risks and benefits of surgery versus conservative management were outlined.
She was given time to consider the risks and benefits before deciding.

Synonimy: to confirm comprehension

I checked her understanding by asking her to summarise the plan.
It is good practice to check understanding before ending the consultation.
He checked the patient's understanding of the medication instructions.

Synonimy: lifestyle modification advice

Lifestyle advice was given regarding diet and physical activity.
We provided lifestyle advice to help reduce his cardiovascular risk.
She was receptive to the lifestyle advice offered during the consultation.

Synonimy: adverse effects

I explained the common side effects of the new medication.
He was advised to report any side effects promptly.
No significant side effects were reported during treatment.

Synonimy: to have worries or questions

Please let us know if you have any concerns before the procedure.
She had several concerns, which we addressed in detail.
He was encouraged to raise any concerns at follow-up.

Synonimy: to arrange a review appointment

Please book a follow-up appointment for four weeks' time.
The receptionist will help you book a follow-up appointment on your way out.
He was asked to book a follow-up appointment if symptoms persisted.

notes.front: to put your mind at ease
notes.example:
Synonimy: to reassure / to alleviate worry

I hope this explanation has put your mind at ease.
The consultant's clear explanation put her mind at ease.
We wanted to put his mind at ease before the operation.

Synonimy: to discuss in detail with

Let's go through the results together and answer any questions.
I went through the treatment options with the patient and her husband.
We went through the discharge instructions before she left the ward.

notes.front: to weigh up the pros and cons
notes.example:
Synonimy: to consider the advantages and disadvantages

Take some time to weigh up the pros and cons before deciding.
We helped him weigh up the pros and cons of each treatment option.
She weighed up the pros and cons before consenting to surgery.

Synonimy: in your own time

Please read through the information at your own pace.
Recovery will happen at your own pace, so there's no need to rush.
You can ask questions at your own pace throughout the consultation.

notes.front: is there anything you'd like to ask?
notes.back: czy jest coś, o co chciał(a)by Pan/Pani zapytać?
notes.example:
Synonimy: do you have any questions?

Before we finish, is there anything you'd like to ask?
Is there anything you'd like to ask about the procedure itself?
I paused regularly to check: is there anything you'd like to ask?

Synonimy: chief complaint / reason for presentation

His presenting complaint was a two-week history of cough and fever.
The presenting complaint was acute right-sided abdominal pain.
Her presenting complaint had gradually worsened over several days.

Synonimy: medical background / prior health conditions

His past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes.
There is no significant past medical history of note.
Her PMH is notable for a previous myocardial infarction.

Synonimy: social background

Social history reveals that he lives alone and is independent with daily activities.
Her social history includes a 20 pack-year smoking history.
Social history was unremarkable, with no relevant occupational exposures.

Synonimy: medication history

His drug history includes amlodipine and atorvastatin.
There were no known drug allergies documented in her drug history.
Drug history was reviewed prior to prescribing the new medication.

Synonimy: at the time of admission

On admission, his observations were within normal limits.
Blood tests taken on admission showed a raised white cell count.
She was afebrile on admission but became pyrexial overnight.

Synonimy: provisional diagnosis / clinical impression

The working diagnosis was community-acquired pneumonia.
My impression is that these findings represent a benign lesion.
The initial impression was later confirmed by biopsy.

Synonimy: differentials / possible diagnoses

The differential diagnosis includes cholecystitis and peptic ulcer disease.
Further investigation was needed to narrow the differential diagnosis.
Appendicitis remained high on the differential diagnosis list.

Synonimy: management plan / next steps

The plan going forward includes outpatient follow-up in six weeks.
We discussed the plan going forward with the patient and her family.
The plan going forward is to continue conservative management.

Synonimy: on an outpatient basis

Further investigations can be arranged as an outpatient.
He will continue physiotherapy as an outpatient.
This can be safely managed as an outpatient rather than requiring admission.

Synonimy: to coordinate with / to communicate with

I will liaise with the community team regarding ongoing care.
Please liaise with the patient's GP prior to any medication changes.
The ward team liaised closely with physiotherapy throughout her stay.
